reason: E1 directly supports stress relief at 700 °C for a similar EHEA, and E2 shows heat treatment alters grain boundary distributions in AM material. E3 provides general support for post-processing improving fatigue life and links grain boundary features to fatigue, but does not specifically address the AlCrFeNiSi system or the 700 °C condition. The cited evidence thus supports the core premises, though the specific alloy and exact property improvements are not fully covered.
premises: Low-temperature heat treatment (~700 °C) acts as a stress-relief anneal for additively manufactured eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Heat treatment can reorganize grain boundaries (e.g., alter low-angle grain boundary content) in AM components.
Appropriate post-processing reduces the risk of premature fatigue failure in AM parts.
Microstructural anisotropy and grain boundary characteristics significantly influence fatigue performance in SLM materials.
